about: At the Mass of the Lord’s Supper all three Agnus Dei invocations end with “miserére nobis” — “have mercy on us”. The evening Mass is normally solemn or sung. The priest recites these invocations quietly, and the faithful may sing them. When a Low Mass is permitted, the priest recites them audibly, and the faithful may recite them with the priest at the third degree of participation. The kiss of peace is not given and “Dómine Iesu Christe, qui dixísti” is omitted. “Pax Dómini” and the next two prayers of preparation for Communion remain.

seg.tr: Lamb of God, You take away the sins of the world: have mercy on us.

ex.w001: “Agnus Dei” addresses Christ as the Lamb of God. Agnus has the nominative form here but functions as a direct invocation.
